title: Identifying Code Smells in Customer Loyalty System
question: Review the C++ code snippet below. Which code smell is most prominently exhibited in how the loyalty tier calculation is implemented across multiple classes?
explanation: This code exhibits the 'Shotgun Surgery' code smell. The loyalty tier thresholds (500 for Silver, 1000 for Gold, 5000 for Platinum) are duplicated across several classes: EmailService, AnalyticsService, CustomerSupportService, and MarketingService. If these thresholds need to change, modifications would be required in all these classes simultaneously. This is the hallmark of Shotgun Surgery - a single conceptual change requires changes to multiple classes. To fix this, the tier calculation logic should be centralized in one location, perhaps in the Customer class or in a dedicated LoyaltyTierService, so that changes to tier thresholds only need to be made in one place.
